findings.claim: The run API accepts a client-supplied paired-host admission endpoint, allowing the caller to make UAR POST frozen tool invocations and raw validated arguments to an arbitrary loopback URL they provide.
findings.evidence: create_run deserializes `req.tool_admission` and installs `HttpHostToolAdmissionPort::from_input(input)` as `request.host_tool_admission`; `src/uar/runtime/tool_admission/http.rs` then serializes `PrepareRequest { invocation: &PreparedToolInvocation }`, and `PreparedToolInvocation` includes `validated_arguments`. The only URL validation in `from_input` is loopback `/uar/admission/v1` plus caller-provided Authorization.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not accept `tool_admission` directly from general create-run JSON; construct/install the host admission port only from the authenticated Boss bridge/host-resource path, or bind it to a server-generated capability that untrusted API clients cannot choose.

findings.claim: Boss binds admission to a canonicalized workspace string while UAR is asked to run with the original workspace string, so valid paired runs can fail admission when the two path spellings differ.
findings.evidence: The create-run payload sends `working_directory: session.workspace.path` at line 190, but the bridge admission options use `workspace: realpathSync.native(session.workspace.path)` at line 290; UAR freezes `world_state.directory().display().to_string()` into `ToolAdmissionContext::new` and Boss `UarHostToolAdmission.binds` rejects any invocation whose `workspace !== this.options.workspace`.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one workspace identity for both fields: either send the same canonical path as `working_directory`, or have UAR return/derive the exact workspace string that Boss stores for admission comparison.
